I am 48, been farming this 9.2 mu for 20 years. My old man taught me, and I watch what the neighbors do. I never went to school, but I know my fields.

Last year my cabbage heads were a bit small — not as big as Wang Laoda's from the east end of the village. This year I will put more. I always start with one full bag of compound fertilizer on each mu of cabbage — that is 50 jin per mu — then I topdress with urea twice, half a bag each time. I also throw in some potassium sulfate, one bag spread across two mu, because the input dealer said it makes the heads tight and heavy. I water four times from planting to harvest. I spray four times for cabbage worms and those little green aphids. I plant 3.5 mu of cabbage in spring.

Chinese cabbage is my main money crop — I plant 5 mu after the early cabbage and kidney beans come out. I give it the most fertilizer. One bag of compound per mu at planting, then urea twice, half bag each time, and potassium too. Better too much than too little. A bad harvest means real money lost; wasting some fertilizer is just a cost. I water five times. Spray four times.

Spinach is easy. I plant 3.5 mu in autumn. Half a bag of compound fertilizer at planting, one urea topdress later. Water three times. Spray twice, maybe three if the leaf miners get bad.

Chili — I plant 1.2 mu. I buy hybrid seeds from the seed shop in town, start them under plastic covers, then transplant. Fertilizer like cabbage but I give more potassium for the fruit. Water six times, they need water when setting fruit. Spray five times, chili gets thrips and mites.

Eggplant — 1 mu. Heavy feeder. Same as chili, plenty of compound plus urea and potassium. Water six times. Spray five times.

Kidney bean — 1 mu. Beans fix some nitrogen in the roots, or so people say, but I do not trust that enough to skip fertilizer. I still give half a bag compound per mu and some urea. Water three times. Spray three times.

I rotary till everything. The machine man comes with his rotary tiller, 40 yuan per mu. No point ploughing deep like the old days.

I worry about costs. Fertilizer is expensive now — urea went up again. But losing yield is worse than wasting a bit of fertilizer. I will spend the money. My wife and I do most of the work ourselves, only hire help for transplanting and harvest if we are running late.
